title: Investigate and fix eval fragmentation from prefix truncation in Private pools
creator: Carla Nguyen
description: Several Private (VPC/on-prem) customers reported sudden regressions in automated evals and production prompts after the runtime sampling-defaults rollout (runtime-1.25). Symptoms: short, fragmented completions (sentence pieces dropped), JSON partial outputs, and non-deterministic truncation that varies by request size and pool utilization. This ticket tracks investigation, reproducible test cases, hotfix, canary, and follow-up hardening.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Carla Nguyen: Customer A (private pool) raised an escalation: JSON outputs truncated mid-field starting the morning after runtime-1.25 deployed to private pools. Included their prompt/eval set in a Gist and a short recording. Triage assigned to ENG on-call.

2026-02-26 - Rafael Ortiz: Reproduced locally using customer prompt + same model (open-redwood-13B-8k-quant). When running concurrent requests with autoscaling at low-burst, we observed prefix lengths sometimes reduced by 1-6 tokens before generation. Created deterministic minimal repro that fails ~2/20 runs.

2026-03-01 - Rafael Ortiz: Narrowed to request pre-processing + batching path in private pool runtime. When a request bundle included a user-supplied stop sequence, the routing layer sometimes removed it early to normalize requests. Combined with an aggressive KV-cache eviction path in private pools (prefetch/truncation logic), the effective prefix passed to the runtime lost trailing tokens — causing generators to start in the middle of a token boundary for some tokenizers, producing fragmented outputs.

2026-03-03 - Eng infra note (Simone Park): Sampling-defaults change (soft-top-p fallback when top-k == 0) made the runtime rely on a post-processing stop-sequence honor step rather than early termination in some code paths. That meant truncated prefixes that lost stop tokens could lead to over-generation or wrong cut points. Both changes are safe independently but interact badly in batched/private pools under KV churn.

2026-03-05 - Rafael Ortiz: Implemented local fix that preserves exact client-sent prefix length through batching/merging and defers stop-seq attachment to after batch alignment. Created PR runtime#4512 with unit + e2e tests using customer's eval corpus. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512

2026-03-07 - QA (Lina Ahmed): Run customer eval harness against private pool simulator for 48h. Failure rate dropped from ~8% to <0.2% on repro corpus. Observed small perf regressions in extremely high-batch cases (p95 latency +4ms) due to extra metadata preserved in merge path. Filed follow-up perf ticket (ENG-52930).

2026-03-09 - PM sync (Evan Park): Decided to do a hotfix canary in 3 private pools with high-traffic customers, roll back if error rate rises and otherwise promote to all private pools in next maintenance window. Communicated plan to affected customers and Solutions engineering.

2026-03-11 - Rafael Ortiz: Hotfix deployed to canary pools. Early telemetry: error counts for truncation events dropped to zero in canary. No new customer complaints from canary pools. Preparing rollout playbook and release notes.

2026-03-14 - Carla Nguyen: Customer A confirmed improvements on their eval set after canary. They reported one remaining edge-case tied to a custom tokenizer; recommended short-term workaround (explicitly append sentinel stop token) while we add a tokenizer-aware guard. Added follow-up tasks in comments.

Planned next steps: promote PR to runtime-1.25.1, publish rollback plan, close customer escalations after 72h stable telemetry, and create a postmortem focusing on batching/stop-seq interaction and private-pool KV eviction behavior.
